page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9ae.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T95 processors clocked at 2.25 GHz. It provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs matched with 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 processor-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance operates without discrete GPU acceleration and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for all persistence requirements. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline throughput of 10 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default.

The 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio offers balanced resource distribution without over-indexing on memory or compute capacity. Because the instance lacks bundled local storage, storage performance and latency are entirely decoupled from the host compute infrastructure. The 10 Gbps network baseline facilitates moderate network traffic demands between distributed services or centralized database nodes. From an infrastructure cost perspective, this configuration optimizes spending by dedicating hardware resources strictly to compute and memory, avoiding the overhead of idle NVMe disks or unused accelerators.

This hardware balance positions ecs.g9ae.4xlarge well for medium-tier enterprise applications, multi-threaded backend web serving, application middleware, containerized worker clusters, continuous integration runners, and relational database deployments relying on external block storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9ae.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9T95 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Managed via the KVM hypervisor, it supplies 16 dedicated vCPUs running at a baseline clock speed of 2.25 GHz alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an even 1:4 core-to-memory distribution of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes no integrated GPUs and relies entirely on external network-attached volumes for data persistence due to the absence of onboard local storage. A 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth provides steady transfer capacity for inter-service communication. With its balanced compute-to-RAM design and lack of bundled local disk overhead, the ecs.g9ae.4xlarge delivers a cost-efficient foundation for enterprise middleware, containerized microservices, backend web applications, continuous integration pipelines, and general business workloads requiring consistent dedicated CPU execution.
